unit.title: Clean floors, walls, furniture and furnishings

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Before cleaning a villa's living room, why should you walk round and look at the surfaces first?
options: To count the furniture for the villa's insurance company
To find out which guests have stayed in the villa before
To see what each surface is made of and what it needs
To decide which surfaces can be left until next month

questions.stem: Why must you know what a floor is made of before you clean it?
options: Some cleaners and methods damage some floor types
The floor type tells you how many guests use the room
Every floor type must be mopped with plain bleach
Only wooden floors ever need to be cleaned at all

questions.stem: Which of these can damage (etch) a marble floor?
options: A neutral floor cleaner mixed as the label says
An acid cleaner, or vinegar or lime juice
Clean warm water with a well-wrung mop
A dust mop used dry to pick up grit

questions.stem: Why is too much water bad for a wooden or laminate floor?
options: Water makes wood floors far too slippery to polish
Water washes away the colour of the wood at once
Wooden floors must only be cleaned with bleach
Water can soak in, so the boards swell, lift or stain

questions.stem: What is the first step in cleaning a hard floor?
options: Put floor polish straight onto the dusty floor
Scrub it with the machine and a strong chemical
Mop it with hot water and plenty of bleach
Sweep or dust mop to remove loose dust and grit

questions.stem: Why is grit on a tiled or marble floor removed every day?
options: It makes the floor look a different colour in the sun
Under shoes it scratches and dulls the surface
It blocks the mop bucket when the floor is mopped
Guests prefer to walk on sandy floors near the beach

questions.stem: What is a damp mop?
options: A mop wrung out well, so it leaves the floor only slightly wet
A mop that has been left soaking in the bucket all night long
A mop used only to spread polish on wooden floors
A mop with a dry head, used to collect dust and grit

questions.stem: A villa's terrazzo floor looks dull even after mopping. What usually brings back the shine?
options: Mopping it twice a day with a strong bleach solution
Rubbing it with cooking oil and leaving it to dry
Polishing it with a floor machine and the right pad
Leaving the doors open so the sea breeze dries it

questions.stem: Before using a rotary floor machine (a scrubber or polisher), what should you check?
options: That the floor is still wet from the last mopping
The plug, cable and pad are in good order and fitted right
That a guest is ready to hold the cable for you
That the machine has been left switched on since the last job

questions.stem: When using a rotary floor machine, where should the cable be?
options: In front of the machine so you can see where it is
Wrapped round the handle so it does not trail at all
Under the machine, so it is held flat on the floor
Behind you, over your shoulder, away from the pad

questions.stem: How do you change the pad on a floor machine safely?
options: Switch off and unplug the machine first
Hold the machine still while it is running
Lift the machine with the motor still on
Ask a co-worker to stop the pad by hand

questions.stem: Which machine is used to suck up dirty water after scrubbing a floor?
options: An ordinary dry vacuum cleaner for carpets
A floor polisher fitted with a white pad
A wet-and-dry vacuum (wet pick-up)
A leaf blower used from the doorway

questions.stem: Floor machine pads come in different colours. In general, how do darker pads differ from lighter ones? (Always check the maker's chart.)
options: Darker pads are only for carpets and rugs
Darker pads give a higher shine than light pads
There is no difference; the colour is for looks
Darker pads scrub harder; lighter pads polish

questions.stem: What must you do before using a stepladder to clean a high wall?
options: Stand it on top of a table so it reaches the high part of the wall
Check it is in good order and set it fully open on firm ground
Lean it closed against the wall like a straight ladder
Make sure the top step is free so you can stand on it

questions.stem: When working on a stepladder, how should you reach the part you are cleaning?
options: Lean out sideways as far as you can reach without falling
Stand on the very top step to get closer to it
Keep your hips between the sides; move the ladder
Hold on with your knees so both hands are free

questions.stem: Why should you wear gloves when washing walls with a detergent solution?
options: To protect your skin from the chemical
To stop fingerprints going on the wall
To make the cloth easier to wring out
To keep the detergent warm for longer

questions.stem: A floor cleaner has been put into a spray bottle with no label. What should you do?
options: Smell it to find out what it is, then use it
Use it on a small area and see what happens
Pour it into the mop bucket with the bleach
Do not use it; report it to your supervisor

questions.stem: When you wash a painted wall, why do you test the cleaner on a small hidden spot first?
options: To see how much cleaner will be needed for the whole room
To check it does not take off paint or leave a mark
To let the wall get used to the cleaner before washing
To find out how long ago the wall was last painted

questions.stem: What is the best way to remove a scuff mark from a painted wall?
options: Rub gently with a damp cloth and a little mild cleaner
Scrub hard with a scouring pad and scouring powder
Paint over it with whatever paint is in the store room
Wipe it with neat bleach straight from the bottle

questions.stem: In Jamaica's warm, damp weather, black spots appear on a bathroom ceiling. What are they most likely to be?
options: Dust blown in from the road outside
Rust coming through from the zinc roof sheets above
Mould, which grows in damp, poorly aired places
Marks left by guests' sunscreen

questions.stem: What should you do about mould on a bathroom ceiling?
options: Paint over it with white paint so the guests cannot see it at all
Use the right product and PPE, air the room and report it
Leave it, because mould is harmless to people
Wipe it with a dry duster and shake it outside

questions.stem: How do you remove cobwebs from the high corners of a room?
options: With a wet mop, pushed up into each corner
By spraying them with insect spray and leaving them
By standing on a chair and pulling them off by hand
With a long-handled cobweb brush, from the floor

questions.stem: How should you clean a polished wooden table?
options: Wash it with a wet cloth and leave the water to dry
Scrub it with a scouring pad to remove the old polish
Dust it with a soft cloth and use polish sparingly
Spray it with glass cleaner and leave it in the sun

questions.stem: A guest's cold glass has left a white ring on a wooden side table. What should you do?
options: Wipe it dry, then report it so it can be treated properly
Rub it hard with sandpaper until the ring has completely gone
Pour hot water on it to melt the mark away
Cover it with a mat so nobody ever sees it

questions.stem: Why should you not put too much polish on wooden furniture?
options: Polish makes wood dry out and crack straight away
It builds up as a sticky film that holds the dust
Too much polish changes the colour of the wood to white
Polish is only meant for floors, not for furniture

questions.stem: Metal patio chairs at a seaside villa go rusty quickly. Why?
options: The sun melts the paint on the chairs every day
Guests use them only in the evening
The chairs are cleaned too often with water
Salt in the sea air speeds up rust

questions.stem: How should you care for metal furniture on a villa terrace by the sea?
options: Leave it alone, as metal furniture never needs cleaning
Scrub it with steel wool and bleach every day
Wipe off salt with fresh water, dry it and report rust
Cover it in cooking oil so the rain runs off it

questions.stem: What causes smears when you clean a mirror?
options: A dirty cloth or too much cleaner left on the glass
Cleaning the mirror from the top down to the bottom edge
Using a dry, lint-free cloth to finish
Cleaning it when the room is cool

questions.stem: Which cloth is best for finishing glass and mirrors?
options: A fluffy towel that has been used in the bathroom
A wet cloth taken straight from the mop bucket
An old newspaper soaked in floor polish
A clean, dry, lint-free or microfibre cloth

questions.stem: How should you clean a lampshade made of fabric?
options: Wash it in the sink with hot water and bleach
Remove dust with a soft brush or the vacuum's brush tool
Wipe it with a wet cloth while the lamp is switched on
Spray it with furniture polish and rub it in

questions.stem: Before you clean a table lamp or a ceiling fan, what must you do?
options: Turn it on so you can see the dust more clearly
Spray it with water so the dust does not fly up
Switch it off, and unplug it where you can
Ask the guest to hold it while you wipe it

questions.stem: How should you clean wooden or plastic window blinds?
options: Close the slats and dust or wipe them from top to bottom
Take them down and soak them in the swimming pool
Pull the slats apart and bend each one to shake off the dust
Leave them, as blinds are cleaned only once a year

questions.stem: How should you clean a framed picture with glass in front?
options: Spray glass cleaner straight onto it so it runs behind the glass
Take the picture out of the frame and wash it in water
Wipe it with a wet floor cloth from the bucket
Spray the cleaner onto a cloth, then wipe the glass

questions.stem: How should chrome taps and towel rails be cleaned so they shine?
options: With a scouring pad and powder to remove the shine
With bleach left on overnight so it can soak in
With a mild cleaner, then dried with a dry cloth
With floor polish rubbed in and not wiped off

questions.stem: You scrub a tiled floor by the villa kitchen. Why do you rinse it afterwards?
options: To make the floor wet enough to put the new polish on it
To remove cleaner left behind that can make it slippery
To cool the floor after the hot scrubbing machine
Rinsing is only needed if a guest asks for it

questions.stem: What does "stripping" a floor mean?
options: Taking up all the old tiles so a new floor can be laid
Pulling the carpet off the floor so it can be cleaned
Painting lines on the floor for a dance event
Removing old polish with a strong chemical and a machine

questions.stem: After stripping a vinyl floor, what is usually done before the room is used again?
options: The floor is left bare and rough so that nobody can slip on it
The floor is covered with a carpet to hide it
New coats of floor finish are put on and left to dry
The floor is washed with neat bleach to whiten it

questions.stem: When you are scrubbing a corridor floor that guests use, what should you do?
options: Put out signs and close off the area until it is dry
Ask guests to walk carefully on the wet parts
Work fast and let guests walk across the wet floor
Leave the doors open so the floor dries without signs

questions.stem: A large villa needs its floors stripped and polished. When is the best time to plan this?
options: On the day the guests arrive, so it is fresh for them
When the villa is empty between bookings
During the guests' dinner, while they are in the dining room
At night, while the guests are asleep upstairs

questions.stem: How can you check that a hard floor has been cleaned well?
options: Ask a co-worker to walk on it in wet shoes
Pour some water on it to see how fast it runs off the edge
Rub it with your hand and smell your fingers
Look along it towards the light for streaks, dirt and marks

questions.stem: While cleaning you find a crack in a glass table top. What should you do?
options: Turn the table round so the crack faces the wall
Fill the crack with clear nail polish
Take it out of use if you can, and report it
Leave it, as it is the guest's problem

questions.stem: Before you move a heavy wooden cabinet to clean behind it, what should you do?
options: Empty it, get help, and lift with bent knees
Drag it across the tiles by yourself, still full
Push it over onto its back on the floor
Pull it by the doors so it slides out

questions.stem: Why are neutral cleaners used for the daily cleaning of most floors and furniture?
options: They are the strongest cleaners and remove all stains
They have a strong smell that guests like
They need no water at all, so no rinsing
They are gentle and do not harm most surfaces

questions.stem: After cleaning a room, how should you leave the furniture and furnishings?
options: Pushed against one wall so the floor stays clear
Put back in their usual places, straight and tidy
Out in the corridor until the floor has been checked
Wherever they look best to you that day

questions.stem: What should you do with a floor machine when you have finished?
options: Leave the pad on and stand the machine on it
Wind the cable tightly round the handle while wet
Leave it plugged in at the wall for the next shift
Unplug it, clean it, remove the pad and store it

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the floor machine that spins a pad or brush under it to scrub or polish floors?
Which kind of ladder stands up on its own legs, without leaning on a wall?
What hard floor is made of fired clay tiles with a shiny glaze, and is common in Jamaican kitchens and bathrooms?
What type of cloth, made of very fine fibres, cleans glass without leaving lint?
What is the pH number of a neutral cleaner?
What is the name of the round nylon disc fitted under a floor machine to scrub or polish?
How many points of contact should you keep with a ladder at all times?
What is the name for dusting with a cloth that is slightly wet and well wrung out?
What word is used for polishing a hard floor with a fast-spinning machine to bring up the shine?
What is the general word for a cleaning product, like a liquid soap, that lifts dirt and grease off surfaces?
Which item of PPE protects your eyes when you clean above head height with a chemical?
What hand tool with a long rubber edge is used to push water across a floor to a drain?
What is the name of the wide, flat mop used dry to collect dust and grit from hard floors?
What do you put on wooden furniture, a little at a time, to protect it and give it a shine?
What floor is made of marble chips set in cement and ground smooth, and is found in many older Jamaican homes?

essays.stem: Compare how you would care for three hard floors in a villa: marble, ceramic tile, and wood or laminate.
essays.modelAnswer: All three floors need loose dust and grit removed every day with a dust mop or broom, because grit scratches them under shoes. Marble is soft stone. I damp mop it with clean water and a neutral cleaner made for stone. I never use acid cleaners, vinegar or lime juice, because they etch dull marks into it, and I wipe up spills quickly, especially fruit juice, rum punch and wine. Ceramic tile is hard and glazed, so it is easy to care for. I damp mop it with a neutral cleaner, and I scrub the grout lines when they get dirty, rinsing so no slippery film is left. Wood and laminate do not like water. I use a well-wrung mop or a cleaner made for wood, I never flood the floor, and I dry any wet patch at once, so the boards do not swell or lift. For all of them I follow the maker's instructions and test a new product on a hidden spot first.
markingPoints: Removes dust and grit daily from all three, and says why
Marble: neutral stone cleaner, no acids, wipe spills quickly
Ceramic tile: neutral cleaner, scrub and rinse the grout
Wood or laminate: very little water, dry at once, wood cleaner
Follows the maker's instructions and tests on a hidden spot

essays.stem: Describe how to damp mop a tiled floor in a villa's living room, from start to finish.
essays.modelAnswer: I collect a mop, two buckets, a neutral floor cleaner, a measuring jug, gloves and wet floor signs. I move small furniture and rugs out of the way. I sweep or dust mop the floor first to remove sand, dust and grit, because wet grit turns to mud and scratches. I read the label and measure the cleaner into the right amount of water in one bucket, and put clean rinse water in the other. I put out the wet floor signs. I start at the far side of the room and work back towards the door, so I do not walk on the wet floor. I wring the mop well and move it in a figure of eight, overlapping the strokes, and I rinse and wring it often. I change the water when it gets dirty. I leave the floor to dry, then put the furniture and rugs back. I clean and dry the mop and buckets and put them away.
markingPoints: Prepares equipment, PPE and signs, and moves furniture
Sweeps or dust mops first and says why
Measures the cleaner and uses rinse water
Works from the far side to the door with a well-wrung mop in a figure of eight
Changes dirty water, lets it dry, replaces furniture and cleans the equipment

essays.stem: Explain how to use a rotary floor machine safely to scrub or polish a floor.
essays.modelAnswer: I only use the machine if I have been trained and my supervisor allows it. I read the maker's instructions. Before use I check the plug and cable for cuts or burns, and I check the pad or brush is the right one for the job and is fitted correctly, with the machine unplugged. I clear the area, put out signs and keep guests away. I wear non-slip shoes and, if I use chemicals, gloves and eye protection. I plug in near the area and keep the cable behind me, over my shoulder, away from the pad. I hold the handle firmly with both hands at waist height and start the machine with the pad flat on the floor. I raise or lower the handle slightly to steer it from side to side, working in overlapping strokes. I never leave it running unattended. When I finish, or to change the pad, I switch off and unplug it first. Then I clean the machine and pad and store them.
markingPoints: Trained and allowed; reads the maker's instructions
Checks plug, cable and the correct pad, fitted while unplugged
Clears the area, uses signs and suitable PPE
Keeps the cable behind, holds firmly and steers by raising or lowering the handle
Switches off and unplugs to change pads and when finished, then cleans and stores

essays.stem: Describe the steps to strip and refinish a vinyl floor in a hotel corridor, and explain when this should be done.
essays.modelAnswer: Stripping is done when old polish has built up, gone yellow or worn patchy. It is planned for a quiet time, or when rooms near it are empty, because the corridor must be closed for some hours. I put out signs and close the area. I remove furniture and sweep the floor well. I wear gloves, eye protection and non-slip shoes, because the stripper is a strong chemical and the floor gets very slippery. I mix the stripper exactly as the label says and spread it over a small section with a mop, leaving it the time the label gives, without letting it dry. I scrub it with the floor machine and a dark stripping pad, then pick up the dirty solution with a wet vacuum. I rinse the floor twice with clean water and let it dry completely. Then I put on thin coats of floor finish, letting each coat dry before the next. When it is hard and dry, I put back the furniture and remove the signs.
markingPoints: When: built-up or worn polish, at a quiet planned time
Closes the area, sweeps, and wears gloves, eye protection and non-slip shoes
Mixes stripper as the label says and works in sections without letting it dry
Scrubs with the right pad, picks up with a wet vacuum, rinses well
Applies thin coats of finish, each dried, before reopening

essays.stem: Describe how to wash the painted walls, doors and skirting boards of a guest room.
essays.modelAnswer: I first remove dust and cobwebs with a duster or a long-handled brush, starting high. I protect the floor and furniture with a dust sheet if needed, and I switch off and cover electrical sockets where water could get in, never splashing them. I mix a mild detergent in warm water as the label says, and put clean rinse water in a second bucket. I test the solution on a small hidden spot first to check the paint does not come off. I wear gloves. I use a sponge or cloth that is wrung out well, so water does not run down the wall. I wash a small section at a time, with gentle circles, then rinse it and dry it with a clean cloth before moving on, so there are no streaks or tide marks. I take extra care round light switches, door handles and door frames, where hands leave marks. Last, I wipe the skirting boards and the tops of doors. I report any damaged paint.
markingPoints: Dusts first and protects floor, furniture and sockets
Mixes a mild detergent and tests on a hidden spot
Uses a well-wrung cloth and works in small sections
Rinses and dries each section to avoid streaks
Pays attention to switches, frames and skirting, and reports damage

essays.stem: Explain how to work safely at height when cleaning high walls, ceiling fans and light fittings.
essays.modelAnswer: First I see if I can do the job from the floor with a long-handled duster or brush, because that is safest. If I need a stepladder, I check it before use: the legs, steps, feet and locking bar must be sound, with nothing bent or missing. I set it fully open on firm, level, dry ground, and I keep the area round it clear. Someone can hold it if the Centre's or property's rules say so. I wear non-slip shoes. I climb facing the ladder and keep three points of contact, such as two feet and one hand. I never stand on the top step or the top platform unless the maker allows it, and I keep my hips between the sides of the ladder. I never lean out to the side; instead I climb down and move the ladder. Before I clean a fan or light, I switch it off and let it stop and cool. I never stand on chairs, tables or beds.
markingPoints: Uses long-handled tools from the floor where possible
Checks the stepladder and sets it fully open on firm, level ground
Keeps three points of contact and does not stand on the top step
Never over-reaches; moves the ladder instead
Switches off fans and lights first and never stands on furniture

essays.stem: Describe how to clean and care for wooden furniture in a villa.
essays.modelAnswer: Wooden furniture, such as mahogany tables, dressers and bed heads, is dusted every day with a soft, clean cloth, and damp dusted with a well-wrung cloth when needed, so the dust is picked up and not spread. I never wet wood a lot, and I dry it straight away, because water can leave marks and make the wood swell. I clean sticky marks with a cloth barely damp with mild soapy water, then dry the spot. I use furniture polish only now and then, and only a little, on a cloth, not sprayed on the wood, and rub it in following the grain. Too much polish leaves a sticky film that holds dust. I put coasters under glasses and keep furniture out of strong sun where I can, because the sun fades and dries wood. I check for water rings, scratches, loose handles and signs of termites, such as small holes or fine dust, and I report them.
markingPoints: Dusts daily with a soft cloth; damp dusts with a well-wrung cloth
Avoids too much water and dries at once
Uses polish sparingly on a cloth, with the grain
Protects from glass rings and strong sun
Checks for and reports damage such as rings, scratches, loose parts or termites

essays.stem: Describe how to clean lamps, ceiling fans, framed pictures and blinds in a villa living room safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with the highest items and work down. Before I clean a ceiling fan, I switch it off and wait for it to stop. I use a long-handled fan duster or a checked stepladder, and wipe each blade with a damp cloth so the dust does not fall everywhere. For lamps, I switch them off, unplug them where I can and let the bulb cool. I dust fabric shades with a soft brush or the vacuum's brush tool, and wipe the base with a damp cloth, keeping water away from the wiring. For framed pictures, I spray glass cleaner onto a cloth, never onto the glass, so it does not run behind and spoil the picture, and I dust the frame. I check that pictures hang straight and are secure. For blinds, I close the slats and dust or wipe them from top to bottom, then turn them and do the other side. I report any loose wires, broken bulbs or damage.
markingPoints: Works from high to low
Switches off fans and lamps, unplugs, and lets bulbs cool
Uses suitable tools: fan duster or checked ladder, soft brush for shades
Sprays cleaner on the cloth for picture glass; checks pictures are secure
Cleans blinds with slats closed, both sides, and reports faults

essays.stem: Explain how Jamaica's climate (heat, damp, salt air and sand) affects floors, walls and furniture, and what a cleaner does about it.
essays.modelAnswer: Jamaica is hot and often damp, and many villas are by the sea. Sand is carried in on shoes and blown in by the wind. It scratches tile, marble and wood floors, so I put barrier mats at doors and dust mop the floors every day. Damp air and poor airflow let mould grow on bathroom ceilings, walls, grout and the backs of cupboards. I air rooms, wipe up water, and clean mould early with the right product and PPE, and I report damp patches. Salt in the sea air settles on metal, glass and furniture. It rusts metal patio chairs, fittings and door handles and leaves a film on windows, so I wipe them often with fresh water and dry them. Strong sun fades fabrics and dries out wood, so I close blinds or curtains in the hottest part of the day where the guest allows, and keep furniture out of direct sun. Insects and termites like damp wood, so I report any signs quickly.
markingPoints: Sand scratches floors: barrier mats and daily dust mopping
Damp and heat cause mould: air, dry and clean it early, report it
Salt air rusts metal and films glass: wipe with fresh water and dry
Sun fades fabric and dries wood: shade the room and furniture
Reports insects, termites and damp patches

essays.stem: Explain how you would check your work after cleaning floors, walls and furniture in a guest area, and what damage you would report.
essays.modelAnswer: When I finish, I stand at the door and look at the room as a guest would. I look along the floor towards the light for streaks, dull patches, footprints and missed corners, and under the furniture and behind the doors. I check that walls have no streaks or tide marks after washing, and that there are no cobwebs high up. I run a clean hand or cloth over furniture tops, picture frames and skirting boards to check for dust. I check glass and mirrors from the side for smears. I make sure the furniture, lamps, pictures and cushions are back in their usual places and straight. Then I report any damage I found, such as cracked tiles, chipped marble, scratches or water rings on wood, torn upholstery, peeling paint, mould, rust, loose handles, broken blinds or lamps that do not work. I report on the maintenance form or to my supervisor, saying where it is and what it is, and I do not hide damage.
markingPoints: Checks the room from a guest's view, including corners and under furniture
Checks floors in the light, walls for streaks and glass for smears
Checks for dust on tops and frames and puts furniture back in place
Names suitable kinds of damage to report
Reports on the form or to the supervisor with the location, and never hides damage

practical1.title: Scrub and polish a hard floor with a rotary floor machine
practical1.brief: As a group, clean a hard floor in one of the Centre's training rooms or the mock villa (vinyl or tile, about 20 to 30 square metres) using a rotary floor machine, as you would between bookings at a Jamaican villa. The assessor acts as your supervisor. Work in these stages: (1) look at the floor, find out what it is made of and plan the job; (2) clear the furniture, put out signs and close off the area; (3) check the machine, plug, cable and pads, with the machine unplugged; (4) sweep or dust mop the floor; (5) mix the cleaner as the label says and scrub the floor in sections with the right pad; (6) pick up the dirty water with a wet vacuum or mop, and rinse; (7) when the floor is dry, buff it with a polishing pad if the floor and the Centre's rules allow; (8) check the floor, put the furniture back, and clean and store the machine. Every member runs the machine for part of the floor while the assessor watches, and every member leads at least one other stage. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Rotary floor machine with a scrubbing pad and a polishing pad (or brush), and the maker's instructions
Wet-and-dry vacuum or mop and two buckets
Neutral floor cleaner or scrubbing solution, with its label and SDS, and a measuring jug
Broom or dust mop, dustpan and brush
Wet floor signs and a barrier tape or cones
Gloves, safety glasses and non-slip shoes
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The cleared floor with signs and the area closed off
The machine, cable and pads being checked, unplugged
The floor swept or dust mopped
A member scrubbing with the cable behind them
Dirty water being picked up, then the rinsed floor
The floor buffed (or the dry, clean floor), seen along the light
The furniture back in place and the machine cleaned and stored
checklist: Found out the floor type and chose a suitable cleaner and pad
Closed off the area with signs before starting
Checked the plug, cable and pad, and fitted the pad with the machine unplugged
Swept or dust mopped before wet cleaning
Measured the cleaner as the label says and wore gloves and eye protection
Ran the machine under control, with both hands and the cable behind
Picked up the dirty water and rinsed so no slippery film was left
Checked the finished floor and put furniture back in place
Switched off and unplugged before changing pads, then cleaned and stored the machine
safety: Use the floor machine only as trained and with the assessor watching; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
Switch off and unplug before fitting or changing a pad
Keep the cable behind you and out of the pad's way; stop if the cable is damaged
Keep signs and barriers up until the floor is dry
Wear non-slip shoes, gloves and eye protection with chemicals; never mix products
Lift furniture with help, bending the knees

practical2.title: Clean the walls, wooden furniture and furnishings of a villa living room
practical2.brief: As a group, clean the living room of the Centre's mock villa (or a training room set up as one) to the standard expected before guests arrive. Share out the work so that every member cleans at least one wall section, one piece of furniture and one furnishing while the assessor watches. Work in these stages: (1) walk round, find out what each surface is made of, and plan who does what; (2) remove cobwebs and dust high places with long-handled tools, with the fan and lamps switched off; (3) test a mild detergent on a hidden spot, then wash, rinse and dry a section of wall, a door and the skirting; (4) clean the glass table top, mirror and picture glass without smears; (5) dust and lightly polish the wooden furniture; (6) dust the lamps and blinds, and wipe a metal patio chair to remove salt; (7) check the room as a guest would, put everything back in its place and fill in a damage report for any faults the assessor has set up. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Long-handled cobweb brush and fan duster
Mild detergent, glass cleaner and furniture polish, with labels and SDS
Two buckets, sponges, microfibre and lint-free cloths
Vacuum cleaner with a brush tool
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The group's plan, showing who cleans what
High dusting with the long-handled tools, fan switched off
The tested spot and a wall section half washed, half not
The glass table and mirror finished, with no smears
The wooden furniture dusted and polished
Lamps and blinds cleaned, and the metal chair wiped
The finished room from the door, and the completed damage report
checklist: Found out the surface types and chose suitable products
Worked from high to low and dry before wet
Switched off the fan and lamps before cleaning them
Tested the detergent first, then washed, rinsed and dried the wall with no streaks
Cleaned glass with cleaner sprayed on the cloth and left no smears
Dusted wood and used polish sparingly with the grain
Put furniture and furnishings back straight and in place
Reported damage clearly on the form
Worked safely with the stepladder and took a full part in the group
safety: Do not stand on furniture; use long-handled tools or a checked stepladder, keeping three points of contact
Switch off and unplug lamps and fans before cleaning, and keep water away from sockets
Read labels, wear gloves and never mix products
Lift or move furniture with help, bending the knees
